author: ghackett
body:
## Problem

The sidebar row context menu's "Open In…" submenu (File Manager, Terminal, editors…) always opened the directory the session *started* in. It was built from `session.cwd`, which is the first cwd the transcript records — so a session that later moved into a git worktree or a subdirectory kept handing out its old project directory.

## Fix

Resolve the directory at menu-build time, newest source first:

- **Open tab** — the tab's live `current_agent_cwd()` (read from /proc), via a new `SessionSidebar.live_cwd` callback the window installs alongside the existing `takes_prompt`/`has_changes` ones.
- **No tab** — `resume_cwd()`, the last cwd recorded in the transcript tail. This is the same answer resuming and "Open in Ghostty" already use, and it needs no new persistence: the transcript on disk is the durable record, so the right directory survives app restarts. It also already falls back to the starting directory when the recorded one no longer exists (deleted worktree).

The group header's "Open In…" is untouched — the project root is the right directory there.

## Testing

- `resume_cwd()` tail-scan and fallback behavior is covered by existing tests in `tests/test_sessions.py`; verified the last-cwd + deleted-dir fallback against a synthetic transcript locally.
- Import-checked `sidebar`/`window` under GTK (no local pytest — CI runs the suite).

author: dbwiddis
body:
The Lint job logged **1565 javadoc warnings** on every run. GitHub caps annotations at 10 per check, so that list was pure noise and anything genuinely new was invisible behind it.

## The rule was being enforced by the wrong tool

Almost all of it was doclint's `missing` group demanding a comment on every protected field of the C-struct mirrors and every implicit constructor. That is not the rule this project wants — and it was also the only thing enforcing the rule it does want. Checkstyle had `JavadocMethod`, `JavadocType` and `JavadocPackage`, but those **validate javadoc that already exists**; presence lives in `MissingJavadocType`/`MissingJavadocMethod`, which were not enabled. Nothing would have caught a new undocumented public class.

The two now split the work:

- **Checkstyle owns presence** — `MissingJavadocType`/`MissingJavadocMethod` at `scope=protected`, matching the configuration used by [opensearch-project/flow-framework](https://github.com/opensearch-project/flow-framework/tree/main/config/checkstyle)
- **doclint owns correctness** — `-Xdoclint:all,-missing`, so bad tags, broken `{@link}` and malformed HTML still fail the build

Javadoc warnings drop **1565 → 8**, and the 8 are a pre-existing module-path note about JNA's javadoc being in the unnamed module.

## Scoping the 580 sites this surfaced

| Group | Count | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `jna`/`ffm` binding packages | 334 | Suppressed — mirror C headers field for field, already exempt from `ConstantName`, `MethodName`, `TypeName` for the same reason |
| `*JNA.java` / `*FFM.java` backend twins | 241 | Suppressed — see below |
| Real gaps | **81** | Written in this PR |

The twins are worth explaining. `@Override` is exempt, so almost all implementation code is already covered; what trips the check is the one member that cannot be `@Override` — the public constructor:

```java
public final class MacPowerSourceJNA extends MacPowerSource {
    public MacPowerSourceJNA(String psName, String psDeviceName, double psRemainingCapacityPercent, ...
```

It forwards the full field list to the abstract parent's constructor, which **is** documented here. Documenting 241 of those restates the shared base.

Fields are not checked at all — `MissingJavadocVariable` would want comments on 1293 struct mirrors.

## The 81

76 in `oshi-common` (constructors, factory methods, and 14 hand-written descriptions for the abstract platform bases) and 5 in the Windows registry drivers.

Also collapses a duplicate `JavadocMethod` module — one bare, one configured, both running — into a single one at public and protected scope, and extends the existing test-file suppression to the new checks.

## A measurement trap, now documented

Checkstyle caches per file in `target/checkstyle-cachefile`, so a second run only re-checks what changed; `javadoc:javadoc` likewise skips when `target/reports` is populated. Measuring either without a `clean` first reports a fraction of the real count and looks like a fix. This cost me several contradictory readings before I spotted it, so AGENTS.md now warns about it.

## Verification

Every number above is from a clean tree. Full gate green from clean: install, spotless, checkstyle, forbiddenapis, javadoc, and 1504 tests successful / 0 failed.

## Summary

Three related additions to `@jaypie/llm`, landing together on this branch.

**Mistral provider.** A first-class Mistral adapter and client, `MODEL.MISTRAL` nested under the catalog, a refreshed Fireworks catalog, Grok 4.5, and pricing that no longer follows aliases. Prose-to-schema conversion now runs in a fresh context rather than a corrective turn.

**Exchange capture.** `stream()` emits exchange envelopes like `operate()` does, both accept a caller-supplied `AbortSignal`, and a host may register the exchange store instance directly with `Llm.useExchangeStore(dynamodb)` instead of relying on the dynamic import.

**External tools and suspend/resume (#473).** A tool may declare `external: true` (`LlmExternalTool`, no `call`) to state its execution is owned by the caller. When the model calls one, the loop parks: `operate()` returns `status: "in_progress"` with the outstanding calls on `response.pending` and the exchange envelope attached unconditionally. The envelope's `pending` block is the resume payload and survives `JSON.stringify` across a process boundary. Resume with `operate(undefined, { resume: { exchange, results }, tools })`.

Recorded history became provider-neutral for every provider as part of that work: tool turns enter history as `function_call` / `function_call_output` items, which is what makes a parked envelope re-entrant.

## Supporting packages

- `@jaypie/fabric` 0.3.9 — `fabricTool({ external: true })` emits a call-less external tool; the structural `LlmTool` becomes the same callable/external union
- `@jaypie/dynamodb` 0.6.10 — a parked exchange persists its resume payload under `state.pending`, protected ahead of `historyDelta` in the 400KB truncation order
- `@jaypie/testkit` 1.2.62 — `createMockTool` is typed against the new union; overloads keep every existing form returning `LlmCallableTool`, and `{ external: true }` produces a call-less tool
- `@jaypie/eslint` 1.2.6 — core `no-redeclare` is off for TypeScript, where it cannot read an overload signature and `tsc` already rejects a genuine redeclaration
- `@jaypie/express` 1.2.32 and `@jaypie/fabricator` 0.4.1 — drop the now-unused `no-redeclare` disable comments; no functional change

`npm test` passes for every affected package, and repo-wide typecheck, lint, and build are clean. The live LLM capability matrix passes across all provider shards; the mistral shard needed one re-run after a `Rate limit exceeded` response from the provider.

author: 135crewdog
body:
Players opening the installed PWA got an older cached build, sometimes for
days. Two causes, one of them the supposed fix:

- the browser looks for a new sw.js only on a NAVIGATION (and at most daily),
  so an installed app that is resumed rather than relaunched never checks;
- `autoUpdate` — which sounds like the answer — reloads the page from a
  service-worker event the moment a new build activates. In a permadeath game
  that is an infrastructure event ending a run, and it still doesn't help the
  already-booted page, which runs old code until that happens anyway.

registerType is now 'prompt': a new build installs and WAITS. The composition
root registers explicitly (injectRegister: null, so the plugin injects no
second registration) and checks for updates on boot, on visibilitychange ->
visible, on `online`, and hourly — the first three folded into the listeners
the leaderboard flush already owns. When one is waiting, a dim clickable line
appears under the version watermark; clicking it posts SKIP_WAITING and the
page reloads when the new worker takes control. Nothing reloads on its own.

No "check for updates" button, deliberately: checking is one conditional GET
and the app has four natural moments to do it. A button delegates to the
player a job the page can do itself.

Presentation and tooling only — nothing under core/, world/, entities/,
systems/ is touched and no RNG is drawn, so no balance run.

- vite.config.js: registerType 'prompt', injectRegister null, explicit
  skipWaiting:false / clientsClaim:true (the two switches this rests on)
- src/ui/updateNotice.js: the notice as a pure DOM factory — a live region
  that is empty until there is something to say, a platform <button> for
  keyboard activation, idempotent show(), one apply per click
- src/main.js: registration, the four checks, pagehide teardown
- index.html: the third row of the top-right stack, styled like the Menu text
- tests/ui-updateNotice.test.js: 11 jsdom cases, incl. that a bare keydown
  does NOT apply (pinning the no-hand-rolled-key-handling decision)
- e2e E18: the real round-trip — mutate dist/sw.js, update(), assert the
  notice appears and the page did NOT reload itself, then click and assert it

Third of five, after `site` (#108) and `ansible-tools` (#109).

**This is the most exposed of the group** — it manages *two* OpenShift API-group kinds rather than one: a `Route` **and** a `ConsoleLink`. SSA combined with such a kind is what leaves ArgoCD unable to resolve a `parseableType`, and this app was among the five that silently stopped syncing for six hours on 2026-07-28.

## Two things make this app different — both checked
`gitea` has state and a Job, unlike the previous two:

- **The Job** (`gitea-oauth-provision-{{ .Release.Revision }}`) is a `PostSync` hook with `hook-delete-policy: BeforeHookCreation`, so it's recreated per sync. Job immutability isn't a factor.
- **The PVC** `gitea-data` is `Bound`, 10Gi, `gp3-csi` — and the chart requests exactly `accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]` / that size. The manifest produces no diff against it, so the git data isn't at risk. (PVC specs are largely immutable, which is why this was worth confirming rather than assuming.)

## Pre-state
Deployment `generation=2`, `1/1` ready, pod running **19 days** — considerably older than the 5d4h pods on `site` and `ansible-tools`, so a restart here would be more visible. Gitea keeps its state on the PVC and survives one, and nothing else sources from it (ArgoCD itself pulls from GitHub, not gitea).

## Standing caveat, unchanged
`site` and `ansible-tools` both migrated with **no rollout and no disruption** — but their field managers were unchanged afterwards (`argocd-controller` still `op=Apply`, no `last-applied-configuration`), so ArgoCD hasn't yet needed a client-side apply on either. What's proven is that comparison keeps working and workloads are undisturbed; the first genuine client-side apply remains untested on all three.

`shared-builds` is still the one real data point in favour — same transition a week ago, and it has since created a BuildConfig through the client-side path cleanly.

`vm-portal` and `rhdh`. `rhdh` isn't in the `bootstrap` values render, so I'll locate its definition before touching it rather than assuming the same edit applies.

body:
Continues the readability work from #93. Both changes are about the same complaint: the diagrams are correct but you cannot *read* them.

## #99 — edges had no visual hierarchy

Every edge was drawn identically, so a utility imported forty times looked exactly like a one-off reference. The graph already knew the difference — `count`, `typeOnly` and `inCycle` are computed during analysis and were discarded at render time.

Measured on this repo's module map (357 edges):

| channel | effect |
|---|---|
| weight from `count` | 4 edges reach the cap; the spine of the codebase becomes visible |
| `typeOnly` muted | **72 edges (20%)** stop competing with runtime coupling |
| `inCycle` coloured | cycles become findable — previously computed, never drawn |

Width is logarithmic (the interesting contrast is 1 vs 10 uses, not 40 vs 50) and capped, so a single hub cannot swamp the picture.

**The rules live in core, not in the renderers.** The webview and the SVG exporter each had their own `edgeStroke`; duplicating the weighting would let the exported picture drift from the on-screen one, which is exactly what the shared layout exists to prevent.

## #98 — folder overviews folded to one useless box

`collapseToFolders` groups by leading path segments, so a `src/`-rooted repo folded to `src` and a monorepo to `packages`. Both true, both useless.

The obvious fix — "pick the first depth with more than one folder" — is *not enough*, and this repo is the counterexample: it has three top-level folders (`examples`, `packages`, `scripts`) that never reference each other. Correct grouping, blank diagram. A useful depth needs more than one group **and edges between them**:

| depth | nodes | edges |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | **0** |
| 2 | 13 | **14** (0 crossings, 553×560) |

Compare the flat module view: 114 nodes, 352 edges, **1,295 crossings**, 7418×2815.

This replaces the extension's local "if depth 1 yields fewer than 4 folders, try depth 2" heuristic — arbitrary, capped at depth 2, and invisible to the CLI and MCP server. The choice now lives in core so every consumer agrees.

- 662 unit tests (up from 644), 28 integration tests, lint and typecheck clean.
- Public-API contract test updated deliberately for the three new exports.
- SVG golden test updated for the new marker; added a test asserting a 16-use edge renders at the cap and a type-only edge stays muted.

author: marcosandremartins
body:
## Overview

Adds PostgreSQL support to Railyin: config-driven database selection (SQLite default, PostgreSQL opt-in) backed by a single async `Db` port that runs on Bun's native `Bun.SQL`. Built from two OpenSpec proposals — `support-postgresql` (feature) and `support-postgresql-tests` (test suite) — both fully implemented and verified in this PR.

## What changed

### Feature (`support-postgresql`)
- `config/database.yaml` (driver-tagged, `+.sample`). **Absent → SQLite default** (`~/.railyn/railyn.db`); present → `driver: sqlite|postgres` selects the engine.
- **Async data layer:** the synchronous `bun:sqlite` runtime was replaced with an async `Db` port (`rows`/`get`/`exec`/`begin`) — two adapters: `SqliteDb` (bun:sqlite-backed, so `:memory:` correctness is preserved) and `PostgresDb` (Bun.SQL-backed). A `Dialect` strategy (`SqliteDialect`/`PostgresDialect`) isolates the SQL that differs between engines: `now()`, `intervalAgo()`, `jsonExtract()`, `returningId()`, boolean mapping. All queries use `$1` positional placeholders.
- **Dialect-aware migration runner:** SQLite replays the 53 existing, checksum-frozen migrations via `bun:sqlite`; PostgreSQL applies one consolidated baseline (`db/migrations-postgres/001_baseline.ts`, 22 tables) via `Bun.SQL`.
- ~60 production files converted to the async port (repositories, handlers, engines, conversation layer, streaming buffers, workflow tools, boot).
- Along the way, fixed 7 real SQLite-only SQL bugs that would have broken on Postgres: `datetime('now', interval)` → `Dialect.intervalAgo()` (5 sites), `INSERT OR IGNORE` → portable `ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING` (2 sites).

### Tests (`support-postgresql-tests`)
- Test harness (`helpers.ts`) migrated to the async port — schema built from the **real** SQLite migrations (no more hand-maintained DDL copy).
- `FakeDb` — records SQL text + params, for pure-unit repository tests with no database.
- `pgTestContainer()` — Docker-gated PostgreSQL testcontainers fixture; skips cleanly with a clear message when Docker is unreachable (verified: exit 0, no hang).
- **PostgreSQL testcontainers tier** (14 tests) runs under vitest/Node rather than `bun test`, because `@testcontainers/postgresql` hangs indefinitely under the Bun runtime (confirmed via direct reproduction — same script resolves in ~1.2s under Node). Uses `NodePgDb` (postgres.js-backed) to exercise the *real* production logic (migration runner, dialect fragments, baseline schema) against a live container.
- Unit-tier coverage: config resolution (15 scenarios), dialect fragments (9), row-mapper type coercion (9), `Db` port contract + provider/DI (11).
- New CI job: `postgres-tests` in `pr-checks.yml`.

## Verification (all green)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `bun test src/bun/test` | 2071 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test e2e/api` | 39 pass, 0 fail |
| `npx playwright test e2e/ui` | 689 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun run test:postgres` (Docker present) | 14 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun run test:postgres` (Docker absent) | 14 skip cleanly, clear message |

## Notes
- No changes to `src/shared/rpc-types.ts` or the frontend — this is a backend persistence swap; the Playwright suite passing unchanged is the regression signal for the frontend.
- `bun:sqlite` is retained deliberately: SQLite migrate-time replay + the `Db` port's SQLite adapter (fixes `:memory:` correctness — `bun:sqlite` and `Bun.SQL`'s own sqlite adapter don't share state).

body:
## Why this file

`didcomm-protocols.ts` sat at **96.2% lines but 38.9% branches** — the signature of code that runs in tests but only ever with one shape of input. Every builder was called with its optional arguments omitted, so each `thid ? { thid } : {}`, optional `comment`, and default parameter had one side that never executed.

Those branches are not incidental. **The threading identifier is what ties a DIDComm response back to its request** — and `requestCredential(thid)`, `mediateGrant(routingDid, thid)`, `keylistUpdateResponse(updated, thid)` and `keylist(dids, thid)` had never emitted a `thid` in any test.

## Result

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `didcomm-protocols.ts` branches | 38.9% | **100%** (36/36) |
| `didcomm-protocols.ts` lines | 96.2% | **100%** |
| repo branches | 83.15% | **83.90%** |

20 tests added (10 → 30). 1,965 passing, eslint clean. Test-only.

## Cases chosen for where this shape of code usually breaks

- **`requestCredential(undefined, comment)`** — a comment with no thid must not invent one. Easy to get backwards with spread-conditionals.
- **`encodeOutOfBandInvitation`** against a base that already carries a query string, exercising the `?` vs `&` separator — plus a round trip through a payload containing `?` and `~`, so the hand-rolled base64url substitution of `+`/`/` → `-`/`_` is actually exercised rather than assumed.
- **`attachedJson`** against malformed messages (`{}`, empty attachments, missing `data`, out-of-range index, `null`) — it parses data that arrived over the wire, so it must return `undefined` rather than throw.
- **`outOfBandInvitation`** with an explicit `accept`, confirming it **overrides** the default rather than appending to it.

## Reading the Coveralls number

Worth recording, since it caused me to misreport coverage repeatedly in earlier PRs: **Coveralls' headline blends lines and branches**:

```
lines    8157/8511  = 95.84%
branches 3483/4060  = 85.79%
combined 11640/12571 = 92.59%   ← the number on the badge
```

So the badge reads ~3pp below the lines-only figure by construction. **Lines are essentially done at ~95.9%; branches are the remaining dimension.** Next largest branch gaps: `keymaster.ts` (148 missed), `herald/routes.ts` (63), `gatekeeper.ts` (21), `mcp-server/tools.ts` (17).

author: nikitakarpei
body:
Implements ADR 0015: delete postings during the distribution cycle once enough holders closer to the posting's DHT position have accepted them. This converges the node's store toward its responsibility range and reduces refresh traffic.

## Summary

The distribution cycle now deletes a posting when at least `YACY_DISTRIBUTION_REDUNDANCY` holders strictly closer to the posting's DHT position than this node have accepted it. This node counts as one of the responsible peers, so peers owe one replica fewer when the node is inside the responsibility window—which prevents deletion of postings the node is responsible for.

The purge runs in the transaction that records the cycle, through the existing `rwipostings.PostingPurger` interface, so the posting observers clear the schedule, the replica ledger, and the offer waits atomically.

## Key changes

- **replicashortfall**: Added `self` parameter to track this node's DHT position. Computes how many replicas peers owe (reduced by one when this node is responsible) and identifies which accepted peers are closer than this node.
- **distributioncycle**: Added `purger` parameter and `handOffPosting` method. The cycle now checks whether accepted recipients include enough closer peers and deletes the posting if so, rather than rescheduling it.
- **Metrics**: Added `rwidistribution_postings_handed_off_total` counter and updated the Grafana dashboard to display handoffs alongside replica drops.
- **Tests**: Added three new cycle tests covering handoff to closer peers, retention when this node is responsible, and retention when only farther peers hold the posting. Updated shortfall tests to verify replica count reduction and ledger window narrowing when this node is responsible.
- **Documentation**: Added ADR 0015 explaining the decision, trade-offs, and limitations. Updated README and specification to reflect that distribution now deletes postings.

## Implementation details

The `ReplicaOffer` struct now carries `HandoffReplicasNeeded` (how many closer acceptances still needed) and `RecipientsCloserThanThisNode` (which accepted peers are closer). The cycle uses these to decide whether to hand off or reschedule.

The `replicasPeersOwe` method reduces the responsibility window size by one when this node is closer than all reachable peers, ensuring the node always holds at least one replica of postings it is responsible for.

No new configuration variable; `YACY_DISTRIBUTION_ENABLED` (off by default) remains the consent to hand postings away.

author: alexander-turner
body:
When the agent tries to end a turn in which it called at least one tool, a new `Stop` hook asks "Are you done with ALL work?" and blocks the stop. The agent ends the check by making `Yes.` the last line of a reply. Any other reply spends one ping and the question comes back, so a session that named work and then stopped gets one more chance to do it.

A turn that called no tool — a question answered, a file explained — has nothing to certify, so it stops with no ping and no extra model round-trip. The check therefore costs nothing on conversational turns.

The loop cannot trap a session. It stops after 3 pings (`_GLOVEBOX_COMPLETION_CHECK_MAX`), `_GLOVEBOX_COMPLETION_CHECK=0` turns it off, and every error path — including a count the hook cannot write — allows the stop.

This is the same shape as Anthropic's `ralph-loop` plugin: a `Stop` hook plus a completion promise. It differs in two ways. It needs no command to arm it, and it re-asks one fixed question instead of replaying an original prompt.

## Review focus

Read `.claude/hooks/completion-check.mjs` first, then `readTurn`. It walks the transcript backwards and must stop at the user prompt that opened the turn; a tool result is itself a user-role entry, so only an entry with no `tool_result` part ends the walk. If that test is wrong, the no-tool exemption reads the wrong turn.

## Decisions made

- **Affirmation matching is lenient.** `**Yes.**`, `yes.` and `Yes` all end the check. A false positive costs one early stop; a false negative holds the session until the ping budget runs out, which is worse.
- **The answer must be the LAST non-empty line.** The word inside a report ("Yes. the tests pass, but …") does not end the check.
- **The budget is 3 pings, then the stop is allowed.** The count resets after each allowed stop, so the next turn starts with a full budget.
- **A count that cannot be written allows the stop.** A counter that never advances would ping forever, so a failed write is the loop's second bound.
- **The hook is dev-only**, like `dev-notes-nudge.mjs`: it is wired into this repo's `.claude/settings.json` and not into the shipped `user-config/settings.json`. It therefore joins the `internal` list in `config/changelog-paths.json` and ships no changelog fragment.
- **The state layer is not extracted into a shared module.** After the simplification it is one 6-line `countAt` plus an inline path, not a second copy of `dev-notes-nudge.mjs`'s four helpers. A shared `lib-session-state.mjs` would have to change that other hook, which this PR does not touch.
- **The hook does not use `agent-control-plane-core`.** That package's `EventKind` has no stop member and its adapters translate tool-call events; this hook exchanges no tool-call verdict.

<details><summary>Verification</summary>

**Files.** `.claude/hooks/completion-check.mjs` (new, 152 lines) and its test file (276 lines); the `Stop` entry in `.claude/settings.json`; the `internal` carve-out in `config/changelog-paths.json`; `stryker.conf.json` (`mutate` from its own generator hook, `tap.testFiles` by hand).

**Size.** The second commit cut the hook from 261 to 152 lines and the tests from 433 to 276, by folding a six-way IO-injection parameter, a transcript tail reader and four state helpers into one `run` that reads real files, and by letting errors propagate to the CLI catch instead of handling each in place.

**Tests: 22 pass, 0 fail** — `node --test .claude/hooks/completion-check.test.mjs`. Observed.

**Coverage: 100% of statements, branches, functions and lines** — `npx c8 --config .c8rc.json --include '.claude/hooks/completion-check.mjs' --all=false --reporter=text node --test .claude/hooks/completion-check.test.mjs`. Observed. The CLI-entry block carries the repo's standard `c8 ignore` and is covered behaviorally by three subprocess tests instead.

**Non-vacuity: five hand-made mutants, each run through the whole test file. All five went red.** Observed.

| mutation | failing tests |
| --- | --- |
| drop the no-tool exemption | 1 |
| `ping > max` → `ping >= max` | 2 |
| ignore a failed count write | 1 |
| never stop the transcript walk at the user prompt | 1 |
| drop the trailing-period leniency | 1 |

**Contract with the harness.** Three tests spawn the hook as Claude Code does, feed a `Stop` payload on stdin, and read stdout: a block decision for unfinished work, empty stdout plus exit 0 after `Yes.`, and empty stdout plus exit 0 on malformed stdin and on a missing transcript.

**CI failure fixed.** `tests/test_stryker_config_completeness.py` failed on the first head: the hook was in Stryker's `mutate` list but its test file was not in `tap.testFiles`, so every mutant was `NoCoverage`. Now green — `uv run pytest tests/test_stryker_config_completeness.py -q`, 148 passed. Observed.

**Local gates.** `bash scripts/precheck.sh` passes over the changed files.

**No stubs.** Every test drives the real module or the real hook process against real files.

</details>

author: shikhergoyal
body:
Found by a security review of the plugin, not by an incident.

## The gap

Provider error text is written by **someone else's server** and was stored verbatim in `provider_keys.last_error`. Several APIs quote the submitted credential in failure messages ("Incorrect API key provided: sk-..."), and this plugin deliberately supports **Custom** and **Local** endpoints whose error text is entirely under a third party's control.

One such reply would have written a plaintext key into the database, and into every backup taken afterwards, defeating the DEK-envelope encryption that protects that key everywhere else.

**Not an exposure today:** `last_error` is never rendered in the admin UI, and mainstream providers truncate keys in errors. This closes the path before it can be used.

## The fix

New `Security/Redactor` scrubs in two layers, because neither is sufficient alone:

1. **Exact removal** of secrets known to have been sent. Format independent, so it covers vendors and self-hosted proxies whose key shape no pattern could anticipate. This is the layer that matters for Custom/Local providers.
2. **Pattern matching** for known shapes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, xAI, Perplexity, Hugging Face, Replicate, bearer tokens) plus a generic 40+ character opaque-token rule for JWTs and base64 blobs. Catches credentials we did *not* send, such as a proxy leaking its own upstream key.

Wired at three points:

| Location | Layer | Why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Errors::message()` | pattern | The single place provider text becomes our message, so every caller inherits it |
| `Gateway::run()` | exact + pattern | Knows the leased key; applies it before the error is stored or returned |
| `Ajax::test_connection()` | exact + pattern | The key under test arrives with the request |

`preg_replace` returning null (backtrack limit on a pathological input) falls back to a **full mask** rather than the unscrubbed original, so the failure mode is losing diagnostics, never leaking a key.

## Deliberately preserved

Ordinary diagnostics stay readable: `Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 20 seconds.` passes through untouched. The 40-character floor sits above any real word and above a UUID (36 chars), so request ids survive for support purposes.

## Verification

- 58/58 `php -l`
- **63/63 unit assertions**, 17 new: every vendor shape, the exact-secret path, the short-string guard (so ordinary text is not mangled), and the UUID / plain-text non-regressions

## Rest of the review

No vulnerabilities found. Zero unauthenticated entry points, all 11 admin-post handlers and 10 AJAX handlers gate on capability + nonce, no SQL injection (every dynamic fragment is int/float cast or a placeholder list), no unescaped output, uploads use `is_uploaded_file()` and are parsed in place, and keys never reach the browser.

body:
## Objective

Implement the first real foreground workflow: an authorized runtime task driven from
`AUTHORIZED` to exactly `PR_OPEN`, and no further:

```text
Authorized Task -> Preconditions -> Registered Branch Preparation -> Claude Implementation
  -> Canonical AgentRunResult -> Deterministic Validation -> Bounded Claude Repair
  -> ApprovalService -> Commit -> Push -> Create Pull Request -> PR_OPEN
```

No CI wait, merge, merge confirmation, baseline update, branch cleanup, runtime closeout, Codex
review/correction, Preparation Mode, Reviewer Mode, AUTO-014, or AUTO-015 behavior is implemented.

## Architecture — `ImplementerModeDriver`

`agentos_workflow/implementer.py` (new) composes only already-delivered subsystems:
`WorkflowSession` (state, locking, durable attempt bookkeeping — AUTO-002), `WorkflowService`
(`invoke_provider` and the five approval operations — AUTO-009/010/012), `agents.
run_deterministic_validation` (unmodified — AUTO-003/005), and the existing Git/GitHub/reporting
Skills. `WorkflowState`'s 19 members and 37 edges, `ProviderRuntime`, both CLI providers,
`ProviderResult`, `AgentRunResult`, and `ApprovalService` are all reused **exactly**, with zero
modifications. One Skill was added, additively: `skills.repository.checkout_stage_branch`
(+56 lines, 0 deletions) — nothing before this checked out a non-baseline, already-created branch.

### `WorkflowService` implementation entry point

No sixth verb was added to `WorkflowService` — its own docstring and `test_service.py`'s
`APPROVED_OPERATIONS`/`FORBIDDEN_OPERATIONS` pins explicitly forbid `implement`. The driver
reaches Claude, Codex, and approvals only through `invoke_provider` and the five existing approval
operations, holding its own `WorkflowSession` alongside for state/lock/attempts.

### `ImplementationTask`

A frozen, `extra="forbid"` Pydantic model carrying everything specific to one run that
`WorkflowSession` itself does not persist for a caller to read back (`workflow_id`, `stage_id`,
contract path/hash, planned branch, baseline SHA, authorization metadata, task description, commit
message, PR title/body). The same object is supplied to both `.start()` and `.resume()`.

### Guarded QA policy

`independent_qa_required` defaults to `true` and resolves through a new, closed
`ImplementerPolicy`/`ImplementerPolicyOverlay` pair, layered `BUILT_IN -> PROJECT -> GATE -> RUN`
exactly like `approvals.resolve_approval_policy`. `false` is refused unless set at the `GATE` or
`RUN` layer — never inherited — mirroring AUTO-012's `AUTO_APPROVE` opt-in discipline exactly.
When QA is skipped, **no verdict is ever fabricated**: no QA report is written, and the approval
gate's own `gate_result` checksum honestly records `qa_performed=false`.

`MACHINE_GATES.md` (1.3 -> 1.4, new §4a) records the Human Owner's explicit authorization of this
guarded exception to its previously-unconditional "QA is never skipped" clause — the same
treatment `HUMAN_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.md` v2.0 §5a gave AUTO-012's approval-gate authorization.

### Canonical `AgentRunResult` integration

Every Claude and Codex invocation goes through `WorkflowService.invoke_provider` ->
`agent_run_result_from_provider_run`, exactly as AUTO-010/AUTO-011 built it. No second
execution-result contract was introduced.

### Deterministic validation pipeline

`agents.run_deterministic_validation` runs unmodified over the working-tree diff. Scope, secret,
and security findings **never** enter bounded repair — they fail the workflow directly.

### Bounded repair

Applies only to tests, lint, formatting, type checking, and completion-report defects; capped at 3
attempts (`config.repair_attempt_limit`); never invokes Codex.

### `ApprovalService` integration at `READY_TO_COMMIT`

The gate runs inside `READY_TO_COMMIT`'s own handler, immediately before `create_commit` is ever
attempted, matching that state's own standing definition (`WORKFLOW_STATES.md` §2: "all
deterministic validation and QA passed; nothing yet committed"). All four checksums
(`repo_state`, `diff`, `agent_result`, `gate_result`) are recomputed and consumed immediately
before staging; any drift invalidates. `PENDING`/`HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED`/`ESCALATED` pause
the driver, resumable. A rejected/changes-requested decision fails the workflow directly, since no
`READY_TO_COMMIT -> REPAIRING` edge exists in `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` and none was added.

### Commit, push, PR creation

`READY_TO_COMMIT`/`COMMITTED`/`PUSHED` share one generic idempotent-retry helper calling
`create_commit`/`push_stage_branch`/`create_pull_request` — all three already idempotent by
construction, bounded to 3 attempts, never blindly retried.

### Resumable stop at `PR_OPEN`

No handler exists for `PR_OPEN` or anything beyond it — calling `.step()` there raises. Every
AUTO-013 state (`AUTHORIZED` through `PUSHED`) has dedicated resume/re-observe logic, covered by
dedicated tests against a real disposable Git repository and stub Claude/Codex CLIs (simulated
crash mid-`IMPLEMENTING`; a pending approval pausing the driver and resuming after a manual
decision).

### AUTO-014 / AUTO-015 confirmation

No CI polling, merge, merge-confirmation, baseline-update, branch-cleanup, runtime-closeout, or
Codex-correction code path exists anywhere in this module — confirmed by grep and by the absence
of any import of `enable_automatic_squash_merge`, `verify_merge_completion`,
`read_required_checks`, `checkout_baseline`, `fast_forward_pull`, `delete_local_branch`,
`delete_remote_branch`, or `generate_closeout_report`.

## Full validation results

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest -q` | 3,484 passed, 0 failed (3,470 baseline + 14 new) |
| `pytest -q -m live_cli -rs` | 32 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `ruff check .` | All checks passed |

| `mypy --strict` | Clean over 123 source files |

| Wheel packaging + out-of-tree import | Verified |

Full evidence and reasoning: `docs/reports/workflow-automation/AUTO-013-completion-report.md`.

## Deferred findings (recorded, not implemented, no GOV stage created)

- **D-14** — `evaluate_initial_execution_failure`'s typed-evidence reconciliation path is
  structurally unusable for `COMMITTED`/`PUSHED` (no authorized GitHub observer yet; a pre-existing
  AUTO-002 gap). Worked around via each Skill's own idempotency.
- **D-15** — `ImplementationDiffEvidence`'s local verifier assumes a pre-commit `IMPLEMENTING`
  design that predates AUTO-013's single-commit-at-`READY_TO_COMMIT` flow.
- **D-16** — QA and stage reports are unsequenced on the very first round (cosmetic only).

Earlier deferred findings (AUTO-012's D-11–D-13, AUTO-011's D-8–D-10, AUTO-010's D-3–D-6,
AUTO-009's D1–D6) remain deferred and untouched.

author: ocalvo
body:
## Summary

Three commands that need no console, so scripts and other programs can drive a session without attaching. None of them registers as a client, so `wmux ls` still reports the session as `detached` and several callers can share one session.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wmux run` | Run a PowerShell command, get its result as CLIXML/JSON/text |
| `wmux send` | Type raw keystrokes (Ctrl-C, prompt answers, TUI input) |
| `wmux capture` | Read the rendered screen as plain text |

## Why `run` exists separately from `capture`

Screen-scraping is the wrong primitive for getting a *value* out of PowerShell. The screen is wrapped to the terminal width, drops whatever scrolled away, flattens the object pipeline to `Out-String` text, and interleaves the echoed command with its own output.

So `run` routes the payload around the terminal entirely: it types a wrapper that serialises the pipeline to a temp file and touches a separate completion marker, then wmux polls for the marker and reads the payload off disk. The terminal only ever carries the command.

```powershell
wmux run -t work --format json -- 'Get-ChildItem src -File | Select Name, Length'
{"Success":true,"Error":null,"ExitCode":null,"Output":[{"Name":"main.rs","Length":12795}]}
```

Results are wrapped in an envelope, so a command that throws is data rather than a parsing failure — and the session stays usable afterwards.

## Motivating case

Keeping shell state across invocations that would otherwise each start cold. Verified by hand: a 2,535-record inventory was built in one process and queried from a completely separate one, with only the three-row answer crossing the boundary.

## Testing

9 end-to-end tests against real detached servers and real pwsh processes, including:

- `run_returns_the_pipeline_as_json_not_a_screen_scrape`
- `run_survives_output_far_wider_than_the_terminal` — 4000 characters through an 80-column terminal, asserted character-exact
- `run_reports_a_failing_command_without_killing_the_session`
- `shell_state_persists_across_separate_send_and_capture_calls`
- `capture_does_not_register_as_an_attached_client`

Plus unit tests for PowerShell quoting, wrapper construction, and the payload-before-marker ordering. `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean.

Follow-up to an incidental finding from #80.

`expected_hardened.test.cpp` only ever used `expected<T, E>` and `expected<void, E>` with a value `E`. Consequently the precondition checks in the `expected<T&, E>` specialization were never compiled at all, and neither the primary nor the void specialization was ever instantiated with a reference `E`. Of the 21 `BEMAN_EXPECTED_TRAP()` sites in the header, only 15 were reachable by any translation unit in the hardened build — the six in `expected<T&, E>` were dead as far as the test suite was concerned.

Adds happy-path coverage for `expected<T&, E>`, `expected<T, E&>`, `expected<T&, E&>` and `expected<void, E&>`, in the same style as the existing sections.

## What this does and doesn't buy

The checks are the same `if (!has_val_) TRAP` shape throughout, so this is mostly about compiling them at all — it is fairly boring, and arguably shouldn't be load-bearing. What it does verify beyond mere instantiation is that the guarded bodies still return the right thing once `T` or `E` is a reference: the shallow-const observers in particular, where a `const expected` still hands out a mutable `T*` / `T&` / `E&`, and where `const E&` with `E = int&` collapses back to `int&`. Those are asserted with `static_assert` alongside the runtime checks.

Happy paths only, matching the rest of the file: a violated precondition traps, and that cannot be observed from inside the process — `__builtin_trap()` kills it with SIGILL before anything can report.

## Verification

Trap sites present in the gcov data for the hardened TU, before and after:

```
before: 15  [943 952 961 970 979 988 1051 1060 1069 1078 1977 2000 2009 2018 2027]
after:  21  [... 2973 2982 3022 3031 3040 3049]
```

Hardened target goes from 5 test cases to 13; full suite 1089/1089 green; `clang-format` clean.

Independent of #80 — no file overlap. Worth noting for whoever merges second: #80 excludes `BEMAN_EXPECTED_TRAP()` lines from the gcovr report by pattern, and that pattern already matches all 21 sites, so the two compose without adjustment.

body:
Closes #188

Parent epic: #183

## Architecture summary

Adds `scripts/finspect`, a PostgreSQL-native operational inspection surface for run/invocation/search history, retained response replay, stable candidate-ID acquisition and retry, extraction-attempt provenance, corpus identity inspection, lossless bounded passages, PostgreSQL full-text search, and bounded literal/regex search.

Target A boundaries remain unchanged:

- PostgreSQL is authoritative for workflow, acquisition, invocation, provenance, corpus identities, retry lineage, and jobs.
- Retained provider bytes remain exclusively in immutable `BLOB_ROOT`; replay verifies both SHA-256 and byte length.
- Qdrant remains a rebuildable projection and is not consulted by these commands.
- Valkey remains optional transient coordination and is not required for correctness.
- Candidate acquisition and retry delegate to `DirectScrapeService`; database/run/schema/blob/privilege preflight completes before adapter construction or Firecrawl/network execution.
- No command accepts scratch directories, result ranks, local payload paths, `_corpus.json`, or file-mediated ingestion manifests.

## Acceptance-review revisions

The follow-up implementation addresses the independent review findings:

- **Lossless bounded retrieval:** cursor v2 is operation- and scope-bound and records intra-chunk offsets. Continuing a clipped passage, lexical result, or pattern result returns the exact remaining suffix without gaps or duplication.
- **Actual token enforcement:** text bounds use each chunk's recorded tokenizer through the tokenizer registry rather than a proportional character estimate; unknown tokenizer identities fail closed.
- **Reused-corpus provenance:** extraction-attempt inspection reads the authoritative committed invocation item associated with `extraction_attempt_id`, preserving source/snapshot/document/derivation/chunk identities when ingestion reused existing records.
- **Bounded public JSON:** nested JSON, text fields, identity arrays, rows, passage characters/tokens, replay bytes, acquisition batches, and final serialized response sizes have explicit limits and truncation/count metadata.
- **Explicit retry:** `retry-candidates` delegates to `DirectScrapeService.retry_failed()`, retries only failed candidate items, and preserves parent-invocation and retry-parent-attempt lineage.
- **Correct process status:** candidate acquisition/retry return exit code `0` only for `status=complete`; partial/failed authoritative results remain on stdout but return exit code `5`.
- **Typed missing IDs:** nonexistent candidate-scoped attempt queries fail with `InspectionNotFoundError`, distinct from an existing candidate with no attempts.
- **Grep compatibility:** `pattern-search --mode literal|regex` preserves case-insensitive literal/regular-expression discovery; `lexical-search` remains explicitly documented as PostgreSQL full-text search.
- **Shared contracts:** cursor encoding, scope fingerprints, tokenizer-aware clipping, bounded serialization, identity-array normalization, and scrape-result normalization are centralized in `inspection_contract.py`.

## Files and contracts changed

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — includes focused unit and disposable-PostgreSQL integration tests in the existing Python 3.11/3.12 repository matrix.
- `docs/database-native-inspection.md` — defines authority, limits, cursor semantics, retry behavior, exit codes, and exact `fread`/grep migration mappings.
- `scripts/finspect` — executable public launcher.
- `scripts/research_store/inspection_contract.py` — versioned scope-bound cursors, exact tokenizer bounds, bounded serialization, and public response helpers.
- `scripts/research_store/inspection_service.py` — service facade for history, replay, scrape, retry, inspection, passages, lexical search, and pattern search.
- `scripts/research_store/inspection_history.py` — bounded run/invocation/response history, verified replay, stable candidate acquisition/retry, and reused-record provenance.
- `scripts/research_store/inspection_corpus.py` — bounded asset inspection, lossless passages, full-text search, and bounded literal/regex search.
- `scripts/research_store/inspection_cli.py` — public subcommands, stable error envelopes, stdout/stderr behavior, and process exit contracts.
- `scripts/test_database_native_inspection.py` — focused unit and failure-boundary regressions.
- `scripts/test_database_native_inspection_integration.py` — disposable-PostgreSQL acceptance coverage.

## Non-goals

- Does not delete `fread`, scratch bridges, compatibility import paths, or persistence-mode configuration; deletion belongs to #189.
- Does not migrate immutable payload bytes into PostgreSQL.
- Does not make Qdrant authoritative or Valkey mandatory.
- Does not add presentation/export files as runtime state.
- Does not refactor the aggregate legacy `research-db` CLI.
- Does not add a new database migration. Attempt-to-corpus lookup consumes existing authoritative PostgreSQL invocation output and falls back to existing ownership columns for older rows.

## Validation

Focused validation:

- `python -m compileall -q /tmp/patch` — passed.
- Focused inspection unit suite — **19 passed in 0.05s**.
- Lossless pagination smoke test reconstructed the complete persisted chunk across clipped pages.

Exact final-head validation for `a850b7cbc4edc679f1d0be8701944daa2d91a8ee` (CI run `30767434119`):

- `ruff check --output-format=github .` — passed.
- `ruff format --check --diff .` — passed.
- Release invariants, Python 3.11 — **66 passed in 0.84s**.
- Release invariants, Python 3.12 — **66 passed**.
- Complete repository matrix with disposable PostgreSQL 16 and Qdrant, Python 3.11 — **1495 passed, 3 skipped in 60.62s**.
- Complete repository matrix with disposable PostgreSQL 16 and Qdrant, Python 3.12 — **1495 passed, 3 skipped in 56.39s**.
- Strict campaign unit/preflight, Python 3.11 — **43 passed, 13 skipped in 1.40s**; disposable-PostgreSQL integration — **8 passed, 2 skipped in 1.72s**.
- Strict campaign unit/preflight, Python 3.12 — **43 passed, 13 skipped in 1.58s**; disposable-PostgreSQL integration — **8 passed, 2 skipped in 1.76s**.
- Research environment adapter, acquisition-authority, authoritative `fsearch`, and authoritative `fscrape` workflows — passed on the exact final head.

No issue-focused test was skipped in the full repository matrix because disposable PostgreSQL was configured. The three broad-suite skips and the strict-campaign skips are pre-existing environment/full-stack skips; no live Firecrawl invocation is performed in CI. Sentinel tests prove candidate lookup and authoritative preflight failures cannot construct or invoke the adapter.

## Migration and compatibility effects

The command surface remains additive for RC-5, but this revision intentionally tightens several public contracts:

- Cursor v2 invalidates previously emitted cursor-v1 values; callers must restart pagination.
- Passage/search continuation is now lossless and scope-bound.
- `chunk_ids` in bounded inspection/acquisition output is represented as an object with `items`, `total_count`, `returned_count`, and `truncated`.
- Partial or failed candidate acquisition/retry now returns process exit code `5` rather than false shell success.
- New `retry-candidates` and `pattern-search` commands are available.
- No database migration or payload relocation is required.

## Residual risks

- Attempt-to-corpus association is read from authoritative PostgreSQL invocation JSON rather than a normalized association table. This preserves correctness for existing Target A data without expanding issue #188 into a schema migration; normalization may be considered in a later issue.
- Case-insensitive PostgreSQL regex search can be expensive on adversarial patterns; execution is bounded by record/output limits and a fixed two-second statement timeout.
- Replay intentionally rejects retained search payloads larger than 4 MiB rather than partial

`drawPiece` 的 `scale` 是屏幕像素常数（两个工具分别传 `42` 和一个常数），直接在屏幕空间应用 —— 相机怎么动棋子都那么大。放大棋盘棋子显小，缩小棋盘棋子溢出格子。

改为从**投影后的格子尺寸**推出：量格心到相邻格心在屏幕上的 x 向与 y 向跨度取平均，乘以一个命名的比例常数。**逐子按它自己所在的格来量**，所以透视深度也算进去了 —— 远排的子本来就该更小（实测近排/远排格边长比 1.36）。

比例 `0.58` 不是拍脑袋：它取自两个工具此前各自手调出来的常数（46px ≈ 0.543、42px ≈ 0.588）的收敛值。

`scale` 保留为可选覆盖 —— 棋子预览页的可辨度网格要用固定尺寸。

这条在阶段 0 的最终审核里就被指出过，我判为「阶段 1 的渲染工作」然后在阶段 1 里没排进去。

## 2. 预置局面被塞进了相机视角控件

工具② 的视角行原本是 **初始 / 别子 / 俯视（顿悟）** —— 前两个是**局面**，第三个是**相机角度**。两个正交的维度合并之后两边都废了：**没法从俯视看别子局面**，而选局面又会悄悄挪相机。

我的 Task 6 原文就是「预置局面（`views` 的 `onSelect` 里加载）」——是我把内容塞进了相机控件。

修法不是挪按钮，是**补上引擎缺的控件类型**。此前引擎只有滑杆、开关、相机视角、页签，没有「一组离散的具名内容」。新增之后：

| 工具 | `views` 现在只剩 | 搬进 `presets` 的 |
|---|---|---|
| 规则与将杀 | `iso` / `top`（`check` 页多一个 `side`，因为它的应手树在抬高的平面上）| 初始、别子、三个易位变体、吃过路兵、升变、将死、逼和、两个基本杀法 |
| 走法几何 | 不变（本就只有相机角度）| 六种棋子（原本是个滑杆 —— 用滑杆选六个具名的东西是同一类错误的温和版） |

自动演示改为巡回**局面**而非视角。这个控件后面三个工具都要用（选棋谱、选算法题），所以做进引擎。

## 一处取舍

原先每个局面自带一套相机取景（`CAM_ZOOM`/`KING`/`QUEEN`），现在局面按设计不再碰相机，这部分精致度有损失、可读性无损失。若实际用起来觉得需要，可以让局面**建议**一个视角而非强制切换。

author: zalts1
body:
`board watch` can be driven with the mouse. Off unless `~/.board.json` sets
`"mouse": true`, because turning it on costs drag-to-select and that is the reader's
trade to make.

    click a row     selects it, exactly as ↑/↓ would
    click it again  focuses its cmux tab, exactly as Enter would
    wheel up/down   steps the selection — and this part works with the setting off

## The argument

**Two clicks, not one.** A click is the only input in this UI that is a position;
everything else is an identity. The first click selects, which pauses the refresh, and
only then is the frame still enough for the second to mean what it looks like.
One-click-to-jump is §7's cursor problem with no defence left — keyboard selection
survives a re-sort because it is keyed on the session, and a coordinate cannot be.

**The hit map comes out of the drawing pass.** `view.FrameHits` returns the frame and,
per line, the key drawn there. Deriving it beside the renderer would be a second copy of
the layout, and the first band to move would leave the two disagreeing with nothing to
notice — the same argument that keeps `DisplayOrder` on the `UI` value the frame gets
(§3). Clicks resolve against the frame **on the screen**, never a freshly computed one.
A miss — header, band heading, legend, below the frame — does nothing.

## The wheel, which turned out not to be about the mouse

Reported as "the wheel used to work great, now it's messed up". Enabling `?1000`
suppresses alternate-scroll: on the alternate screen a terminal has no scrollback, so it
had been translating notches into `↑`/`↓` and board had been reading them as ordinary
keys, never knowing the wheel was involved.

Binding it back exposed the real number. A probe on the alternate screen, one line per
`read()`:

    mouse off   9 reads, 9 sequences, over 0ms   ESC[B ESC[B ESC[B …
    mouse on    9 reads, 9 sequences, over 0ms   ESC[<65;65;18M …

**One flick is nine events either way, inside the same millisecond.** So the nine-row
jump was never a mouse bug — it is what board has done since long before this branch,
on the default path. `stepClock` collapses it: one step per 5ms over all four step keys,
arrows and wheel alike, deliberately blind to which. The window is sized against the
fastest key repeat any supported machine can produce (10ms on X11, not macOS's 15ms),
with the bias set by the failure modes being unequal — too small moves a flick a few
rows, too large drops keystrokes and reads as broken.

This was fixed twice from the symptom before anything was measured, and a revert that
changed nothing was the evidence that should have stopped it. `EVIDENCE.md` §9.32 records
that, the three broken probes it took to get a measurement — including one that could not
be quit on a Hebrew layout, a case §7 already documents — and the rule it leaves: when a
revert does not move the symptom, stop fixing and start measuring.

## Verification

`gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -count=1 ./...` clean. Golden frames unchanged — `Frame` is
now a wrapper over `FrameHits` and is byte-identical, pinned by a test.

New pure seams, per §11: `FrameHits` (asserted against the frame it returns — every
mapped line must draw that row's label, at every trim and fold), `sgrMouse`, `hitAt`,
`stepClock`.

By hand in a pty against a fixture `$HOME`: enable and disable sequences emitted once
each, a click landing on the intended row, a second click acting on it, three misses
doing nothing, and — on both encodings — nine events in one burst moving one row while
four bursts 300ms apart move four.

## Record

`DESIGN.md` §7 gains the mouse subsection (including why hover and the horizontal wheel
are declined) and §11 the new seams; `EVIDENCE.md` §9.32; README gains the keys, the
config key, and what it costs you.

author: luminabrands
body:
Two separate mobile bugs, both reported from a real device.

## 1. The keyboard (the bigger one)

The phone takeover panel was `height: 100dvh`. **`dvh` follows the URL bar but not the software keyboard.** So on iOS the panel kept its full height with the bottom half underneath the keys; Safari then scrolled the focused input into view, carrying the header and the entire message list off the top of the screen. What was left was an empty black panel with just the input and the legal line sitting above the keyboard.

Only `visualViewport` reports the keyboard, so the takeover now takes its height and offset from there — re-fitting after focus, because the keyboard animates in a frame or two behind the focus event.

Gated on `!MOUNT` plus the 520px query, so the inline hero mount, desktop, and browsers without the API all keep the CSS default.

Measured at 390×844 with a simulated 336pt keyboard:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| panel height | 844 (halfway under the keys) | **508** |
| header | scrolled off the top | **held at y=0** |
| message area | not visible | **355px** |
| input | only thing on screen | **y 437–477, above the keyboard** |

## 2. Long answers landed at their last line

Separate issue, found first. The hero panel gives the message list ~300px; a step-by-step answer runs ~1000px. Scrolling to the bottom put the reader past the instructions — step 1 was 750px above the fold, with only the video links and feedback chips visible.

Messages taller than the pane now align their top. Anything that fits still scrolls to the end, so short replies and the visitor's own messages are unchanged.

`scrollTop` after an answer: 766 (of 766 max) → **322**, the top of that answer.

## What I could not verify

**Neither fix was tested against real iOS Safari** — no device here, and this sandbox's Chromium can't raise a software keyboard. The keyboard fix is exercised by driving `visualViewport` directly, which proves the code path but not the platform. Worth a check on the phone that produced the screenshot before this is trusted.

I also could not view the original screen recording: no H.264 decoder and no ffmpeg in this environment.

## Regression checks

Inline hero mount still mounts, expands and answers in both themes, zero JS errors. Desktop panel unchanged. `assistant.js` string literals still pure ASCII (Shopify charset constraint).

## Intent

The code-metrics workflow ranked `check_schema_field_primitives` as the highest-complexity production function, with ABC 191.2. It coordinated schema composition resolution, direct and nested primitive validation, decoded-field state, format-specific rules, and diagnostic fallback in one control flow, making each schema extension expensive to review.

Separate those concerns into field-kind checks while keeping the public orchestration entry point responsible for schema and field ordering.

## Consequences

Schema field analysis now has explicit boundaries for composition eligibility, direct primitives, nested lowercase primitives, binary composite fields, and format-neutral fields. Language behavior and diagnostic contracts are unchanged. The orchestration function and all newly introduced helpers are below the configured ABC warning threshold.

## Risks

The main risk is changing the order in which diagnostics are emitted or decoded fields become available to later fields. The helpers retain the original call order and share the same decoded-field map; the schema-heavy semantic and generated toolchain tests exercise those paths.

Docs and CHANGELOG only. No code changes — `git diff --name-only` is three files.

## What this is

`docs/M3-CLOSEOUT.md` was written on 2026-07-27 as a gap analysis: every M3 checkbox was ticked, but three of M3's five maintainer tests exercise the *app*, and the app called none of the M3 machinery. That plan has now been followed to the end. This turns the document from a plan into the record of what was missing and what closed it.

Verified against `main` at `92c586a`: `cargo test --workspace` green — **414 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored** (the Welch goldens waiting on M5).

## M3's maintainer test, as of merged `main`

| Test | Status | Gated by |
|---|---|---|
| First plot ~2 s, indexing continues | **Passes** | `first_plot` bench |
| Scroll/zoom 30 s → no stutter, memory under cap | **Passes** | `memory_gate` at 4 GB; `time_view_render` p99 gate (in-memory files only — #107) |
| One-sample spike visible at every zoom | **Passes** | decimation golden — spike preservation |
| Zoom all the way in → individual samples | **Passes** | decimation golden — convergence |
| Close and reopen → opens instantly | **Passes, with a documented residual** | both reopen integration tests; #106 |

## The one judgement call

**M3 closes with the CSV re-parse residual documented rather than staying open for it** — the maintainer's decision, recorded in §6.1 with the reasoning.

A reopen serves both derived caches from disk, so the plot is instant and the index is not rebuilt. The file's *text* is still parsed on every open, so encoding, delimiter, per-row typing and the `InferenceReport` are re-derived each time. body:
CLAUDE.md described the two execution tiers as differing in where their *dependencies* come from. The more important difference went unrecorded: **they run in different Python interpreters, and only the subprocess tier honours the one picked in Settings.** So "switch Python" has only ever switched half the app.

That isn't a footnote — it's the shape of a recurring class of bug:

- **#122 is exactly it.** A venv with `aadc` installed was selected, and the live engine kept reporting `aadc is not installed`.
- The **CA dir has the same asymmetry**: subprocess runs re-point on their next launch, the in-process engine caches CA's modules and needs a restart.
- Someone editing CA can't see their edits in the sliders without restarting — only in analysis runs.

Anyone meeting one of these without the context reads it as a new defect and fixes a symptom. So it's now stated, together with the target — **one interpreter for everything, via a persistent simulation worker** — and the constraints that fix must respect:

- keep the in-process path as the fallback when no interpreter is configured (the frozen app's default, so nothing regresses for users who never open Settings);
- launch through `runtime_paths.default_python()`, **never** `sys.executable` — in a bundle that relaunches the GUI;
- persistent, not per-request: the expensive thing is the model compile, so a fresh subprocess per slider drag would recompile every time.

Replaces an unmerged README paragraph on the same subject (`docs/readme-python-setup`, a leftover from #51). It belongs in CLAUDE.md rather than the README: the README describes what the app does, and this describes what it does wrong.

Docs only — no code, no test changes.

Implementation plan and smoke runbook for [#25 — Encrypt the local database at rest](https://github.com/lhpaul/personal-finances/issues/25). Refactor item: there is no spec, so the issue body is the brief.

- Plan: `docs/specs/developments/20260802195509_25-encrypt-local-database/2_25-encrypt-local-database_implementation-plan.md`
- Runbook: `docs/testing/mobile/25-encrypt-local-database.smoke-test.md`

## The research question, answered

The dispatch asked whether `expo-sqlite` can genuinely encrypt at rest, or whether this needs a native-dependency escalation. **It can, and it needs no new dependency** — but it does need a native rebuild.

Verified against the installed `expo-sqlite@16.0.10` source rather than assumed:

- `node_modules/expo-sqlite/vendor/sqlcipher/sqlite3.c` — **SQLCipher 4.7.0 is already vendored** in the installed package.
- `plugin/build/withSQLite.js` — the `useSQLCipher` prop writes `expo.sqlite.useSQLCipher` into the gradle and Podfile properties; the podspec then compiles the SQLCipher source with `-DSQLITE_HAS_CODEC=1 -DSQLCIPHER_CRYPTO_CC`, and `android/build.gradle` swaps `SQLITE3_SRC_DIR`.
- The Android 16 KB page-size fix for `useSQLCipher` landed in **16.0.9**, so the pinned 16.0.10 includes it.

**`PRAGMA rekey` is disqualified.** `exsqlite3_rekey_v2` returns `SQLITE_MISUSE` on a plaintext database ("rekey can't be used on an unencrypted database"), and SQLCipher's own PRAGMA error text says: *"Use sqlcipher_export() and ATTACH to convert encrypted/plaintext databases."* The plan follows that instruction.

## Approach

Two filenames and one commit marker, rather than encrypting in place:

- `finanzas.db` (legacy plaintext) is copied into `finanzas.enc.db` with `ATTACH … KEY` + `sqlcipher_export()`.
- The copy is verified **on device, in production** with `findPreservationViolations` — the census comparator `db:check` mode 3 already ships — before anything is deleted.
- An `app_settings` row (`encryption_migrated_at`) inside the encrypted store is the commit point. The plaintext original is never mutated and is deleted only after the replacement is verified.
- A pure six-state resolver derives the correct action from what is on disk, so every crash point resumes correctly across process death. Each crash window is mapped to a resolving state and covered by a test.

**No Drizzle migration is added**, so non-negotiable #5 is satisfied structurally and `db:check` modes 0-3 pass unchanged. The schema is byte-identical on both sides; only the container changes.

Key: 32 bytes from `expo-crypto`'s CSPRNG, raw hex, in `expo-secure-store` under `db_key:main`, stored `AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` so a background wake can still open the store. Never in SQLite, never derived from anything in the repo, never logged.

**Complexity: L.** Small code volume, but this is the only change that can irreversibly destroy user data, it crosses a native boundary no JS test can reach, and it edits surfaces owned by #8, #9 and #19.

## Key risks

| # | Risk | Mitigation in the plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | JS ships to a binary built without `useSQLCipher`; plain SQLite **silently ignores** `PRAGMA key` and the store stays plaintext while the app reports success | A `PRAGMA cipher_version` capability probe fails the launch loudly. **No plaintext fallback exists in the code.** Runbook Step 7 asserts this |
| R2 | The database key is lost or replaced while an encrypted store holds data — irreversible total loss | One-way generation rule: the key is generated only when absent **and** no encrypted content exists. The `unrecoverable_key_missing` state fails closed and never deletes the store |
| R3 | Crash mid-migration | Two files, one marker, plaintext never mutated; every crash window mapped to a resolving state and tested |
| R4 | `sqlcipher_export` copies something subtly wrong | The census gate runs on device on every migration and blocks the commit point on any finding. The user's data is protected by a runtime check, not by a test |

## Testing honesty

`better-sqlite3` has no SQLCipher, so the Node tier runs unencrypted and the plan says plainly what it does *not* prove. Three properties are device-only, each with a numbered runbook step: that `PRAGMA key` encrypts, that `sqlcipher_export` copies faithfully through a codec, and that a wrong key is rejected.

What Node *does* prove: the six-state resolver, resume and abort paths, the census gate, the fail-closed key branches, the wipe ordering, and — via a pure `statements.ts` module plus a contract test — the **exact SQL text** the device will execute, so a malformed `PRAGMA key` literal fails in Jest even though its effect cannot be observed there.

## Cross-item consequences

- **#19's wipe** must delete the database key. `collectCredentialKeys` becomes `collectSecureStoreKeys`, and the key is deleted **after** the store file — deleting it first and then failing to delete the file would brick the profile with no recovery.
- **#19's `secure-store-key-namespace.test.ts`** fails by design when a second key namespace appears. This item pays that debt in the same change, with ten enumerated matcher cases.
- **#9's `SecureStorePort.setItem`** gains one optional accessibility argument, defaulting to #9's current behaviour so no #9 call site changes.

## Sequencing

This item must land **last among the data-layer items**, after #10's sync engine and the screens are stable. Sequencing is the orchestrator's call, but the plan's **Implementation Step 0** is a hard landing-tree verification gate that turns each dependency into a concrete file check. A missing seam is a stop-and-report, not a stub.

## Document Quality Gate

- Spec/brief coverage: **Checked** — all three brief acceptance criteria map to implementation steps, named Node unit tests, and numbered runbook steps via an explicit AC-to-evidence table.
- Implementation-order consistency: **Checked** — a scripted cross-section pass over repeated symbols found and fixed five contradictions before commit (step-range heading `1-14` → `1-15`; `deleteDatabase` → `deleteDatabaseIfPresent` in the Decision 6 sequence; a missing `exec` member on `CipherHandle` used by that sequence; `ensureDatabaseKey` and `migratePlaintextToEncrypted` bound to their decisions; the probe key-fingerprint referenced by the runbook but absent from Decision 12). All 12 decision indices resolve, all 30 Verification Log references resolve, and the six `EncryptionState` values are spelled identically in every section.
- Verification support: **Checked** — 30 Verification Log rows at revision `3ac49ee`. Every claim about SQLCipher availability, `rekey` semantics, `sqlcipher_export` copy scope, connection caching, `deleteDatabase` behaviour and WAL state cites the vendored source or the installed package, not documentation from memory.
- Behavioural guarantees: **Checked** — idempotency is attributed to the on-disk commit marker plus the six-state resolver (not to a promise); single-flight to the existing module-level memo in `runtime.ts`; "no data loss" to the census gate that runs before the commit point.
- Complex workflow decision-gate matrix: **Not applicable** — this plan changes product code only; it adds and modifies no workflow decision gate, protocol, status label or mirrored workflow surface.
- Parser/API/concurrency checklist: **Checked, two of the three apply.**
  - *Parser-risk*: applicable narrowly — the plan widens the accepted grammar of #19's `setItem` source-text scanner. Ten enumerated edge cases (hard-coded literal, template literal, comment, self-referencing string literal, two calls on one line, multi-line call, `deleteItem`) each mapped to a named unit test.
  - *Concurrent-event-source*: applicable — launch, background wake (#18) and wipe teardown share the memoized handle. All seven checklist items answered, including cross-process re-entrancy, which a promise cannot guard and which is resolved from disk instead.

## The headline: the descent bench was measuring a fiction

The descent bench's region-conditioned **"with"** arm called `generate_image` with the region crop as a `reference_url`. But fal's text-to-image endpoints **silently ignore `reference_urls`** (accept-but-drop, same as the fresh-gen nano endpoints per PR #109). So the arm that was supposed to prove region-conditioning helps was actually **unconditioned** — a fresh generation wearing a reference URL — and `place_lift` sat structurally ~0.

**Fix:** route the with-arm through the seam the product actually ships, with the crop as the edit **SOURCE** so reference pixels bite:
- interior chains → `build_enter_instruction` + `edit_image` on the `enter_scene` model
- exterior closeups → `build_zoom_instruction` + `continue_image` (Kontext), the closeup rung

Two regression guards (`test_with_arm_rides_edit_seam_not_generate`, `test_exterior_with_arm_rides_zoom_continue`) spy on which seam fires, so the with-arm can never silently slip back to `generate_image`.

## Five hardening themes riding along

1. **Coordinate-scale ladder → shared module.** Extract the fraction/percent/per-mille coercion out of `llm/click.py` into `providers/coordinate_scale.py` and wire it into `detector.py` + `llm/extraction.py` (was click-only). Closes the long-standing "world extraction/detector have the same scale flip" coverage loss — pixel-looking coords now drop instead of edge-clamping.
2. **Enter-retry model swap** (off by default). `ENTER_RETRY_MODEL_SWAP` keeps attempt 0 on the router's production pick and swaps only *judged retry* attempts to a cheaper `nano-banana-2/edit`, threaded via a new `render_for_attempt` hook through `render_loop` → `tap` + both benches. An explicit request-level `image_model` override is respected on every attempt.
3. **Judge transport hardening.** Pillow-downscale the VLM judge payload (`VLM_JUDGE_MAX_SIDE_PX`/`VLM_JUDGE_JPEG_QUALITY`) and route the judge call through `_create_with_retry`. Multi-MB bench JPEGs were large enough inline to reset OpenRouter/Gemini reads; falls back to the original bytes if Pillow can't decode.
4. **Web: disable prefetch/precompute warming in World Mode.** World taps route through geometry / cold resolver context, but the precompute effect was seeding candidate-only warm entries carrying stale `enter_as`/`place_form` classifications. `worldEnabled` now early-returns from both the precompute effect and the hover-prefetch handler.
5. **Bench ergonomics.** Artifact reuse (`*_REUSE_ARTIFACTS`), arm/case filters (`VIEW_BENCH_ARMS`/`VIEW_BENCH_CASES`), style-ref compaction before fal upload, judge retry+backoff, positioning-probe toggle.

Env docs updated in both `.env.example` files; `conftest.py` scrubs the two new env vars.

## Verification

- Backend: **983 passed, 2 skipped**, coverage **86.71%** (floor 85; new `coordinate_scale.py` + `model_router.py` at 100%).
- Web: `tsc --noEmit` clean; pre-commit `eslint --fix` + `ruff --fix` clean.

## Not in this PR

The **live descent-bench run** that empirically proves `place_lift` now lifts post-fix is **not** included here — it costs real fal image + VLM judge spend. Happy to run it as a follow-up (with `DESCENT_BENCH_REUSE_ARTIFACTS` off for a true measurement) once someone confirms the fal balance.

## What's in this PR

Replaces the placeholder tax/compliance-firm marketing copy that shipped in the initial scaffold with the actual Pinnacle Management Ventures content and site structure, mirrored from the live Base44 site (`pinnacle-venture-flow.base44.app`) but now hosted on our own Cloudflare stack — not on Base44.

**New public pages**
- `/services` — overview grid of all 7 services
- `/services/:slug` — detail page per service (Consulting, Funding & Capital, Property Management, Mobile Notary, Property Inspections, Document Courier, Administrative Support) with highlights + "ideal for"
- `/about`
- `/service-area` (on-site South Florida / remote nationwide)
- `/contact` — working request-service form (name, email, phone, service, message)

**Home page** rebuilt to match the real hero copy ("Professional support. Wherever business takes you."), the 7-tile service grid with Popular badges on Consulting and Funding & Capital, and the "Ready to Get Started" CTA band.

**Header/Footer** shared across every public page: Services / About / Service Area / Contact nav, Client Login, Request Service CTA, and the exact notary/legal disclaimer text from the live site.

**Backend**
- `POST /api/contact` — public, IP-throttled (10/hr), writes to a new `contact_inquiries` table
- `GET/PATCH /api/admin/inquiries` — staff/admin can review and triage submissions; added an **Inquiries** tab to the staff console nav
- Migration `0003_realign_services.sql` — replaces the placeholder tax/compliance service catalog seeded in `0002` (which predated having the real business content) with the actual 7 services and matching onboarding questions
- Migration `0004_contact_inquiries.sql` — new table for the contact form

## Verified
- `npx tsc -b` — clean
- `npm run build` — succeeds

## Remaining setup before this is live
1. Apply `migrations/0003_realign_services.sql` and `0004_contact_inquiries.sql` to the production D1 database, in order, after `0001` and `0002`
2. `0003` does a clean replace of `services` / `onboarding_questions` / `client_services` / `client_onboarding_responses` — confirmed safe pre-launch since no real client has signed up yet, but **do not run this against a database with live client signups** without adapting it first
3. Same as PR #1: merging to `main` triggers the existing Cloudflare Pages auto-deploy
4. Phone number and a few operational specifics (exact South Florida coverage area) were carried over verbatim from the live site's public content — worth a human once-over before launch in case anything there was a placeholder

author: mashrafeearyan
body:
# Summary

This pull request introduces the initial runtime architecture for Friday.

The current implementation establishes the basic execution loop:

```
User Goal
    ↓
Take Screenshot
    ↓
Send Goal + Screenshot to Gemini
    ↓
Gemini Generates Python
    ↓
Execute Python
    ↓
Take New Screenshot
    ↓
Repeat Until Complete
```

## Changes

* Added `model.py`

  * Handles communication with the Gemini API.
  * Maintains the AI conversation.
  * Returns generated Python code.

* Added `computer.py`

  * Captures screenshots.
  * Executes the Python code generated by the AI.

* Added `prompt.py`

  * Defines the system prompt that instructs Gemini how to control the computer.
  * Establishes the behavior and rules for the AI.

* Added `main.py`

  * Implements the main execution loop.
  * Connects the model, computer, and prompt components.

## Notes

This is the first working architecture for Friday. The focus of this pull request is simplicity. Friday is responsible for providing the AI with the current computer state and executing the generated Python code, while the AI performs all reasoning and decides how to accomplish the user's goal.

Future pull requests will expand the computer interaction capabilities, improve prompt quality, and make the execution loop more robust.

The run-former already absorbed `#+ATTR_*` lines but dropped their values. This branch records them org-element-faithfully and proves every byte against live Emacs:

- **AST**: `AttrLine{Backend, Value}` / `Affiliated.Attrs` — per-backend ordered raw lines, lowercase backends, org's exact affiliated-ATTR shape (`ATTR_[-_A-Za-z0-9]+`; dual-suffix/bad-charset lines stay standalone keywords, Emacs-verified via a dedicated adversarial fixture).
- **Export-side helpers**: `AttrValues` + `AttrPlist` — a deliberately consumer-friendly reading of `org-export-read-attribute` (quotes unquoted, quote-aware tokenization, later-wins matching the ox-html pipeline; deviations enumerated in the doc comment, verified against live ox).
- **Dump + oracle** emit ` :attr_<backend> ("v1" …)` under one fixed byte-equality rule (alphabetical backends, source-ordered values); goldens refrozen from Emacs 30.2 / org 9.7.11 — including 11 adversarial fixtures whose ATTR values were silently dropped until now.

Downstream driver: personal-site's asset-rendering spec consumes `AttrPlist("html")` for `:width`/`:height`/`:align`. Note: this branch also carries the two previously-unpushed Walk commits (its ancestors).

author: ralvarez83
body:
Sustituye la SPA de React + Vite servida con Docker y Nginx por un sitio estático en Astro publicado en Netlify desde GitHub Actions.

## Por qué

El CV es contenido estático: no tenía más estado que un conmutador de idioma. Aun así enviaba **283,92 kB de JavaScript** (89,22 kB comprimido) al navegador para pintar texto que no cambia, y mantenerlo en línea exigía contenedores, un reverse proxy y renovar el certificado TLS a mano. De hecho el certificado caducó y la web quedó dando aviso de conexión insegura.

| | Antes | Ahora |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | 283,92 kB | Sin bundle de framework; solo un script en línea para recordar el idioma |
| URLs | Una sola, idioma en estado interno | `/` y `/en/`, indexables |
| Aspecto | 4 hojas CSS, una de ellas muerta | Tokens semánticos + variantes `data-theme` |
| Despliegue | Docker + Nginx + TLS manual | Estático en Netlify, certificado gestionado |
| Pruebas | Ninguna | 31 end-to-end |

## Verificación de paridad

Antes de tocar nada se capturó una baseline del sitio React original (commit `710265a`): capturas a página completa en ES y EN sobre tres anchos, más el volcado de textos, enlaces, imágenes y encabezados. El contraste contra la versión migrada dio **0 enlaces perdidos, 0 imágenes rotas y 0 errores de consola**.

Las únicas diferencias de texto son correcciones deliberadas de fallos que arrastraba el original:

- `<html lang>` y `<title>` no cambiaban con el idioma.
- La sección de idiomas incrustaba un encabezado `Idiomas` en español que se duplicaba con el título traducido de la sección: en inglés se leía "Languages" seguido de "Idiomas".
- Los niveles de idioma y el propio "Inglés" se mostraban en español en la versión inglesa.
- `xUnit` figuraba dos veces en las habilidades.
- El subtítulo de "Experiencias anteriores" empezaba por `" | "` al no tener empresa.
- `photo.jpg` se resolvía por ruta relativa y se habría roto en `/en/`.

## Sistema de diseño

El aspecto sale de tokens semánticos declarados en `src/styles/globals.css`. Los componentes no contienen ningún color ni medida literal, así que se puede recambiar la apariencia sin abrirlos. Las variantes `friki` (por defecto) y `serious` recogen la intención de los antiguos `cv-friki.css` y `cv-serious.css` como bloques `data-theme` que solo redefinen lo que cambia. Documentado en `docs/design-tokens.md`.

## Despliegue

El sitio se compila en Actions y se sube ya construido con la CLI de Netlify, sin usar su integración Git: así no hay despliegues duplicados, no se consumen los minutos de build del plan Free y nada se publica si fallan las pruebas.

Este PR debería generar una **previsualización en Netlify**; solo `main` publica en producción.

## Notas de revisión

- **Astro 7, no 6.** La rama 6 arrastra tres avisos XSS de severidad alta sin corregir. `npm audit` da 0 vulnerabilidades.
- **Lucide 1.x eliminó los iconos de marca**, así que los logotipos de GitHub y LinkedIn pasan a componentes propios con el SVG oficial.
- **Las pruebas de regresión visual quedan fuera del CI** (etiqueta `@visual`): el dibujado de fuentes varía entre entornos y compararlas contra capturas hechas en otra máquina daría falsos fallos. Se ejecutan en local con `npm test`.
- **`nginx-reverse.conf` se retira**, aunque enrutaba también `adguard`, `movie-info` y `datos-auto-evaluacion`. Queda recuperable en el commit `e42ed50` para cuando se muevan esos servicios.
- **Queda pendiente** limpiar del historial la clave privada TLS subida por error en `f75ff90`. Se retira aquí del árbol de trabajo; su certificado ya está caducado.

## Después de mezclar

Revisar la URL `*.netlify.app`, luego añadir el dominio personalizado, cambiar el DNS en IONOS y dar de baja el VPS.
